newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Cocoa - Prices fall on mid-crop supply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Cocoa - Prices fall on mid-crop supply.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices continued to fall this week on ample supplies from the country's mid-crop, which more than offset reasonable demand from the main U.S. market and from Europe, traders said on Wednesday.
Domestic prices were quoted at between 2,760-2,775 rupiah a kg, compared with 2,775-2,800 rupiah a kg last week in Ujung Pandang, the trading centre for the growing area of Sulawesi.
"The ample supply on the back of the mid-crop in Sulawesi has dampened sentiment and pushed prices lower," one trader with a Jakarta-based firm said.

Another Jakarta-based dealer said market talk of the loading of around 4,000 tonnes of cocoa at the south Sulawesi city of Ujung Pandang bound to Europe this week would only lend limited support to the market.
"Possible (price) rises due to the loading are likely to be limited as demand is seen remaining weak," the dealer said, adding that details of the deal were not known.

Indonesia's cocoa output in the 1995/1996 (October/September) season, is expected to be higher than the previous period, with traders' estimates ranging between 260,000 and 300,000 tonnes compared with 250,000 tonnes in 1994/95.
